en: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā under the Goatherd’s Banyan tree, having recently attained full enlightenment.
Now at that time, the Blessed One had been sitting for seven days in a single cross-legged posture, experiencing the bliss of liberation.
Then, with the passing of those seven days, the Blessed One arose from that concentration.
Then a certain brahmin, who was habituated to making sounds of approval (*huṁhuṅkajātiko*), approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.
When they had concluded their polite and courteous conversation, he stood to one side. Standing to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One:
“In what way, Master Gotama, is one a brahmin, and what are the qualities that make one a brahmin?”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“The brahmin who has warded off evil states,
who is free from grunting and free from impurity, self-controlled;”
One who has mastered the Vedantas and lived the holy life may rightly proclaim the doctrine of Brahma,
he for whom there is no inflation anywhere in the world.
